findings.issue_text: MySQL no-op UPDATE returns 0 affected rows (changed rows, not matched rows, since CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS is not set), so the rowsAffected == 0 check conflates 'device unknown' with 'device known but nothing changed' and spuriously returns ErrDeviceLimitReached for existing devices when parallel requests in the same second write identical values

Count-then-act race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: CountDevices is followed by a separate insert/update with no transaction, lock, or unique-guard, so N concurrent first-seen devices all pass the check when count == limit-1 and overshoot the device limit

TagDevice moved from a background goroutine (context.Background, 2-minute timeout, recover()) into the synchronous Authenticate path: DB latency/outage now stalls every anonymous request, panics in tagging propagate into the request, and the local cache is only populated on successful tagging so blocked devices execute COUNT + UPDATE on every request

The 1-minute future tolerance in updateDevice (updated_at BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1min) blocks existing devices whose stored updated_at was written by an instance with clock skew >1 minute (or drifted outside the window), incorrectly returning ErrDeviceLimitReached

Frontend type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number | undefined, but the backend DTO field AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 lacks omitempty so the JSON always contains 0 when unset; consumers checking === undefined or using ?? default to detect 'no limit configured' will silently misbehave

Unauthenticated attackers can exhaust the device limit with un-rate-limited requests (no cookies required, fresh ID generated per request), locking out all new anonymous users for up to 30 days (indefinitely with one refresh per device per <30d), with the lockout amplifying into sustained DB load since every anonymous request executes a COUNT over the 30-day window plus a 0-row UPDATE

TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: CountDevices and the insert are separate non-transactional statements with no lock or serialization, so concurrent first-time devices can all observe count < deviceLimit and overshoot the hard cap by an arbitrary multiple

ErrDeviceLimitReached is a plain fmt.Errorf sentinel rather than a typed authn error, so the lockout likely surfaces as an opaque 500/401 with no machine-usable signal for the frontend instead of a meaningful 'device limit reached' response

Device tagging moved from fire-and-forget goroutine (with background context, 2-minute timeout, and panic recovery) to synchronous DB work in the authentication hot path, so DB latency/failure now directly adds latency to anonymous auth and a panic in TagDevice would propagate into the auth path

updateDevice's 1-minute future window (updated_at BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1min) rejects active devices when the previously tagging replica's clock is more than 1 minute ahead of the current replica, misclassifying legitimately active devices as 'limit reached' and locking them out once the cap is full

P1 — Once the device limit is reached, every uncached-device request runs an unindexed full-table COUNT(*) on anon_device (no index on updated_at, only the device_id PK), and rejected devices are never negatively cached because the error path returns before localcache.Set, so the same device re-runs the O(deviceLimit) scan plus a doomed UPDATE on every request, synchronously in the auth path

P2 — Device tagging was moved from a fire-and-forget goroutine (with 2-minute timeout and panic recovery) to a synchronous call in the authentication hot path; every anonymous request that misses the 29-minute local cache now blocks on DB round trips, the 2-minute timeout is gone (the call inherits request-context cancellation), and DB slowness directly inflates authentication latency even when device_limit is unset

P2 — Limit enforcement is check-then-act: CountDevices and the subsequent insert run in separate DB sessions with no transaction, lock, or counter guard, so concurrent first-time tags can all observe count < limit and proceed to insert; the per-instance local cache in HA setups widens the race window, allowing a burst of new devices to overshoot device_limit by an unbounded amount

P2: `anonymousDeviceLimit` response shape drift — TS type `number | undefined` promises `undefined` as the meaningful 'unset' state, but the non-pointer `int64` Go field with no `omitempty` always serializes a number (0 when unset), making `undefined` only reachable against older backends; `0` is ambiguous (server-side means 'unlimited' but consumers may read it as 'zero devices allowed'), so either make the Go field `*int64` + `omitempty` or type the TS side as plain `number` and document `0 = no limit` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200, pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195)

P2: Raw internal sentinel `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` now crosses the authn boundary with no caller/HTTP mapping — no HTTP status, no user-facing message, no wrapping into an authn error type, so devices at the limit get generic unauthenticated treatment (login redirect / 401 / 500 depending on route) with no 'device limit reached' signal (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-49)

P2: `TagDevice` error contract widened from swallowing errors to propagating every error, but the pre-auth-hook caller registered in `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` (`authBroker.RegisterPreAuthHook(a.tagDevice, ...)`) was not updated to tolerate it — a transient DB error during tagging now fails the anonymous request (and potentially session-authenticated traffic if the hook runs for non-anonymous identities), where previously it was logged and access continued (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:144-148)

P3: Device tagging moved inline onto the authentication hot path, losing isolation — the goroutine + `context.Background()` + 2-minute timeout + `recover()` were removed, so tagging (cache-miss ⇒ COUNT query plus upsert) now runs synchronously inside `Authenticate` with the request context, putting DB latency on every anonymous request's critical path, allowing client disconnects to cancel tagging mid-flight, and letting panics in the tagging path propagate into the auth flow and fail the request (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-52)

P3: Limit enforcement is check-then-act — `CreateOrUpdateDevice` counts devices then inserts if `count < limit`, so two concurrent requests from two new devices at `count == limit-1` both pass the check and both insert, making the configured limit soft; worth at least a comment or an atomic guard if exactness matters (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:~119-129)

P3: New `auth.anonymous.device_limit` config key is read via `MustInt64(0)` but absent from `conf/defaults.ini` (and docs), making it invisible to admins browsing shipped defaults / generated config documentation, unlike every other `auth.anonymous` key (pkg/setting/setting.go:1656)

Synchronous DB calls added to the authentication hot path: TagDevice was previously fire-and-forget with a dedicated 2-minute timeout and recover(), but is now called synchronously inside Authenticate with only the request context, so every cache miss performs a CountDevices query plus an upsert before identity is returned, creating a hard synchronous dependency on DB availability with no dedicated timeout or circuit breaker
Tagging is now aborted if the client disconnects mid-request (previously completed in background), slightly undercounting devices

TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: the limit check (CountDevices) and insert are not atomic (no transaction, lock, or atomic guard), so N concurrent first-time devices can all read count < limit and all insert, silently overshooting the configured device limit

No negative caching/backoff for limit-reached devices: the local cache only short-circuits successfully tagged devices, so once the limit is reached every request from a blocked device re-executes CountDevices plus a doomed UPDATE, converting all new anonymous traffic into 2 DB queries per request and adding sustained DB load exactly when the system is at capacity

Bare ErrDeviceLimitReached returned from Authenticate with no defined HTTP mapping: it is a plain fmt.Errorf outside the authn error taxonomy, and behavior depends on how pkg/services/authn handles an unrecognized client error, potentially returning 500s instead of a graceful block/redirect

rowsAffected == 0 conflates 'not found', 'stale', and 'no-op update' in updateDevice: on MySQL (second-precision DATETIME, affected-rows-not-found-rows semantics), two near-simultaneous tags of the same device produce identical row values, causing RowsAffected() == 0 and spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that exists and is in-window

Panic containment regression in the auth path: the defer recover() that guarded the tagging goroutine was removed with the goroutine itself, so a panic inside TagDevice/store code now propagates through Authenticate into the request handler and fails the request (500 via recovery middleware) instead of proceeding anonymously

Core success path of the device limit feature is never tested: an existing, active device re-tagging itself once the limit is full is never exercised; updateDevice's success path (rowsAffected > 0) is never executed, so a regression in the SET clause, WHERE device_id match, or error/success branching would lock out every existing anonymous user while the suite stays green; the test also never asserts post-conditions (updated_at/client_ip/user_agent refresh, no duplicate row, device count stays at limit) (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-69, database.go:72-115) [P1]

The updated_at BETWEEN predicate in updateDevice is completely untested: in the only test reaching updateDevice, the incoming device_id never matches any row, so the test outcome is independent of the BETWEEN clause (inverted bounds, wrong constant, or wrong column would still pass); no test covers device_id matching with stored updated_at outside the 30-day window (should return ErrDeviceLimitReached) or inside it (should succeed) (database.go:74-84) [P2]

No test that expired devices stop counting toward the limit: no test creates a device with updated_at older than 30 days and verifies a new device can be created under a full-looking limit; if the CountDevices window regressed to counting all devices regardless of age, the limit would permanently freeze after the first N devices undetected (database.go:118-127) [P2]

Behavioral change in Authenticate (TagDevice moved from fire-and-forget goroutine to synchronous auth path, and ErrDeviceLimitReached now propagates out of Authenticate) has zero test work: no test verifies Authenticate returns the error when the limit is hit, the caller-visible outcome (401/429/500/fallthrough handling of this non-standard error in the authn pipeline), or that non-limit tagging errors still don't break authentication (client.go:35-52) [P1]

TagDevice now returns errors instead of swallowing them, but the new error contract is untested: updated TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag cases only assert require.NoError on success paths; no test asserts errors are returned to the caller (e.g., invalid/short device ID cookie), leaving callers relying on the old never-fail behavior unprotected (impl.go:143-150) [P2]

Config wiring (device_limit ini → Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit → ProvideAnonDBStore) is untested end-to-end: service-level tests use setting.NewCfg() (limit defaults to 0 = disabled) and the store-level test passes the limit directly, bypassing the wiring; a regression that always passes 0 (silently disabling the feature) would be invisible to the suite; negative values silently treated as 'no limit' are also untested/undocumented (setting.go:1649-1655, impl.go:37-42) [P2]

Count-then-insert race in CreateOrUpdateDevice allows exceeding the limit: CountDevices and the insert run as separate, non-transactional statements, so concurrent requests when count == limit-1 can both observe count < limit and both insert; no test documents or exercises concurrent behavior (database.go:118-127) [P3]

Zero-rows-affected conflation ('no match' vs 'no change') untested under MySQL semantics: rowsAffected == 0 is mapped to ErrDeviceLimitReached, but on MySQL an UPDATE matching a row yet changing no values reports 0 affected rows (without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS), so a device re-tagging with identical client_ip/user_agent and unchanged second-precision updated_at could be falsely rejected; no test covers re-tagging an existing device with unchanged values (database.go:92-101) [P3]

P1: Device limit is bypassed by a simple retry — TagDevice writes the device to the local cache (SetDefaultInt64) before the DB write, so a rejected write (ErrDeviceLimitReached) leaves the device cached; subsequent requests hit the cache and succeed without touching the DB, letting blocked devices in for the 29-minute cache window

P2: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice — CountDevices and the INSERT run in separate sessions with no transaction, lock, or admission record, so concurrent first-tags from multiple new devices all read count < limit and all insert, overshooting the limit

P2: Anonymous authentication now performs synchronous DB I/O in the request path — the fire-and-forget goroutine (context.Background + 2-minute timeout + panic recovery) was removed unconditionally, so every cache-cold anonymous request blocks on CountDevices (a COUNT over anon_device with no index on updated_at) plus the upsert with no explicit timeout, even when device_limit = 0

P3: ErrDeviceLimitReached never reaches the user — the authn service logs client errors and continues to the next client, ultimately failing with a generic 'credentials missing' 401/redirect to login, so blocked users get no explanation and operators cannot distinguish limit-reached from an auth outage; the anonymousDeviceLimit frontend field is unused for messaging

P3: rowsAffected == 0 is overloaded in updateDevice — on MySQL (default changed-rows semantics, second-precision DATETIME), an UPDATE matching an existing fresh device can round to the same stored second (e.g., same device tagged on two instances within the same second) and report 0 affected rows, falsely rejecting the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the code treats `rowsAffected == 0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. But an `UPDATE` can legitimately report 0 affected rows even when the row exists and the `WHERE` clause matches, if the new values are identical to existing values (a no-op update). Since the `SET` values come from the passed `device` (and could be the same across parallel/duplicate requests), this logic conflates “no matching row (or outside time window)” with “matched but unchanged”, causing spurious `ErrDeviceLimitReached` and, via `client.go`, potentially failing anonymous authentication when at the device limit.

TagDevice moved from a background goroutine (context.Background, 2-minute timeout, recover()) into the synchronous Authenticate path: DB latency/outage now stalls every anonymous request, panics in tagging propagate into the request, and the local cache is only populated on successful tagging so blocked devices execute COUNT + UPDATE on every request

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Anonymous.Authenticate` changed from spawning a goroutine with `context.Background()` + a 2-minute timeout + `recover()` to calling `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). This means tagging now runs on the request path (so DB latency/outages can stall anonymous requests) and there is no panic containment (any panic in `TagDevice` would propagate). Also, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can now do `CountDevices` and then `updateDevice` when `deviceLimit` is reached (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go); if tagging errors out, any local-cache short-circuit in `TagDevice` is less likely to be reached/recorded, potentially causing repeated DB work for repeated attempts. These are real, diff-grounded operational/architecture concerns, but not a strictly provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a contract mismatch: frontend config types/runtime initialize `anonymousDeviceLimit` as `number | undefined`/`undefined` (`GrafanaConfig` and `GrafanaBootConfig`), while backend always emits `anonymousDeviceLimit` as an `int64` with no `omitempty` and defaulting to 0 via `MustInt64(0)` and `FrontendSettingsDTO` (`json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"`). So the JSON response will include `0` when not configured, never `undefined`/missing. The claimed consumer misbehavior (checks for `=== undefined` / `??`) isn’t shown in the diff, so it’s not a provable defect here, but the type/API inconsistency is real and could confuse or lead to subtle client assumptions.

The finding’s broader claim about it surfacing specifically as an opaque 500/401 and lacking a machine-usable frontend signal depends on error-to-HTTP/authn mapping not shown in the diff, but the core review concern (non-typed/non-structured error propagation making it hard to produce a specific response) is grounded in the change.

That means the auth request now waits for TagDevice (which performs DB work via the anon store) and any DB slowness/errors will add latency before returning the identity (even though most errors are only logged). The diff also removes the explicit panic recovery wrapper around TagDevice, so any panic inside `TagDevice` (or its callees) would no longer be contained to a goroutine; while the diff doesn’t prove TagDevice can panic, the removal of recovery is a real architectural/perf concern grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly makes anonymous device tagging synchronous in the auth path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go: removed goroutine/timeout, now calls TagDevice(ctx, ...) directly and may return ErrDeviceLimitReached), and when a device limit is configured and reached, every CreateOrUpdateDevice call will execute CountDevices over a 30-day updated_at window before attempting an UPDATE (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). That creates a plausible per-request performance hotspot once the limit is reached. However, the finding’s claims about the COUNT(*) being “unindexed full-table” and that rejected devices “are never negatively cached because the error path returns before localcache.Set” aren’t verifiable from the shown diff (no schema/indexes or localcache set-path shown here).

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` replaces the previous fire-and-forget goroutine (with `context.WithTimeout(..., 2*time.Minute)` and panic recovery) with a synchronous `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` call inside `Authenticate`. This means `Authenticate` now waits for tagging work to complete on cache misses, and the explicit 2-minute timeout is removed (it now relies on the incoming request context). Even when `device_limit` is 0, tagging still runs synchronously and can add DB latency to the authentication path; errors are mostly logged and ignored, but the blocking behavior remains. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a verifiable correctness bug.

adjudication.rationale: In `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`, limit enforcement is implemented as a separate `CountDevices(...)` call followed by the normal insert/update path if `count < s.deviceLimit` (lines added in `database.go`). The count and the subsequent insert/upsert are not in the same transaction/session and there is no locking/unique counter mechanism shown, so concurrent requests can both observe `count < limit` and each proceed to insert, causing the `device_limit` to be exceeded. The diff does not add any DB constraint or transactional guard to prevent this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: `anonymousDeviceLimit` response shape drift — TS type `number | undefined` promises `undefined` as the meaningful 'unset' state, but the non-pointer `int64` Go field with no `omitempty` always serializes a number (0 when unset), making `undefined` only reachable against older backends; `0` is ambiguous (server-side means 'unlimited' but consumers may read it as 'zero devices allowed'), so either make the Go field `*int64` + `omitempty` or type the TS side as plain `number` and document `0 = no limit` (packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200, pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go:195)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a contract mismatch: TS `GrafanaConfig` adds `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and `GrafanaBootConfig` initializes it to `undefined`, implying `undefined` is an expected/meaningful state on the frontend. But the backend `FrontendSettingsDTO` adds `AnonymousDeviceLimit int64 `json:"anonymousDeviceLimit"`` (non-pointer, no `omitempty`) and `readAuthSettings` sets `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = ...MustInt64(0)`, so responses will always serialize a numeric value (defaulting to `0`). Also, server logic treats `0` as “no limit” (`if s.deviceLimit > 0 { ... }`), which is a semantic that should be explicitly reflected in the TS type/docs or by making the Go field optional. This is a real, diff-grounded API shape/semantics issue, but not a directly provable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does widen error propagation in `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice`: after `a.tagDeviceUI(...)` fails it now `return err` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go, near the added `return err`), whereas previously it only logged and continued. However, the claim that this definitively “fails the anonymous request” via the `authBroker.RegisterPreAuthHook(a.tagDevice, ...)` path is not directly verifiable from the diff because the `a.tagDevice` hook implementation and the auth broker’s error-handling semantics are not shown. What is verifiable is a behavior/contract change that warrants auditing hook/caller expectations, but the concrete failure mode described is speculative from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Device tagging moved inline onto the authentication hot path, losing isolation — the goroutine + `context.Background()` + 2-minute timeout + `recover()` were removed, so tagging (cache-miss ⇒ COUNT query plus upsert) now runs synchronously inside `Authenticate` with the request context, putting DB latency on every anonymous request's critical path, allowing client disconnects to cancel tagging mid-flight, and letting panics in the tagging path propagate into the auth flow and fail the request (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-52)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` removes the goroutine, `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ...)`, and `recover()` wrapper and replaces it with a synchronous call `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inside `Authenticate`. This makes device tagging run on the authentication path with the request context (so cancellation/deadlines can abort it) and eliminates the panic isolation that the `recover()` provided. Whether this is a functional “bug” is not provable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded architectural/performance/regression concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Limit enforcement is check-then-act — `CreateOrUpdateDevice` counts devices then inserts if `count < limit`, so two concurrent requests from two new devices at `count == limit-1` both pass the check and both insert, making the configured limit soft; worth at least a comment or an atomic guard if exactness matters (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:~119-129)

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the limit is enforced via a separate `CountDevices(...)` call followed by the normal insert/upsert path when `count < s.deviceLimit` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). Because the count and the subsequent insert are not done atomically (no transaction/lock/unique guard tied to the limit), two concurrent requests can both observe `count == limit-1` and both proceed to insert, exceeding the configured `deviceLimit`. This makes the new `AnonymousDeviceLimit` enforcement potentially incorrect under concurrency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: New `auth.anonymous.device_limit` config key is read via `MustInt64(0)` but absent from `conf/defaults.ini` (and docs), making it invisible to admins browsing shipped defaults / generated config documentation, unlike every other `auth.anonymous` key (pkg/setting/setting.go:1656)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new config field/key being read (`cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)`) but it does not include any changes to `conf/defaults.ini` or documentation files. Since the finding’s core claim is that the key is absent from shipped defaults/docs, that cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous DB calls added to the authentication hot path: TagDevice was previously fire-and-forget with a dedicated 2-minute timeout and recover(), but is now called synchronously inside Authenticate with only the request context, so every cache miss performs a CountDevices query plus an upsert before identity is returned, creating a hard synchronous dependency on DB availability with no dedicated timeout or circuit breaker

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes Authenticate from spawning a goroutine with a separate 2-minute context timeout and panic recovery to calling TagDevice synchronously on the request context (anonimpl/client.go: removed goroutine/timeoutTag; now `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)`). TagDevice ultimately hits the DB via `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(...).CreateOrUpdateDevice` (anonimpl/impl.go wiring now constructs the DB-backed store), and with `AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0` it can additionally execute `CountDevices` before updating/inserting (anonstore/database.go). This creates a synchronous dependency on DB responsiveness/availability in the auth path and removes the dedicated timeout/recover behavior. However, it’s not a strictly verifiable “bug” from the diff alone (it may be intentional to enforce device limits), and the finding slightly overstates that CountDevices happens on every cache miss (it’s conditional on deviceLimit > 0).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tagging is now aborted if the client disconnects mid-request (previously completed in background), slightly undercounting devices

adjudication.rationale: In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go`, the tagging call was changed from a goroutine using `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ...)` to a synchronous `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)`. If `ctx` is request-scoped (as is typical for authn flows), it may be cancelled when the client disconnects, causing `TagDevice` to abort and the device not to be recorded—whereas previously tagging could still complete in the background. This is a real behavior change that could lead to undercounting, but it’s not provably a defect without intended semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice: the limit check (CountDevices) and insert are not atomic (no transaction, lock, or atomic guard), so N concurrent first-time devices can all read count < limit and all insert, silently overshooting the configured device limit
matched_golden_ids: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes a TOCTOU race where concurrent requests can all pass the device count check and then insert, exceeding the limit, and recommends atomicity via transaction/lock—same underlying race condition as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No negative caching/backoff for limit-reached devices: the local cache only short-circuits successfully tagged devices, so once the limit is reached every request from a blocked device re-executes CountDevices plus a doomed UPDATE, converting all new anonymous traffic into 2 DB queries per request and adding sustained DB load exactly when the system is at capacity

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds a per-request device-limit enforcement in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`: when `deviceLimit > 0` it always calls `CountDevices(...)` and, if at/over limit, calls `s.updateDevice(...)` which executes an `UPDATE` and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `RowsAffected()==0` (e.g., for a new/blocked device). In `anonimpl/client.go`, `TagDevice` is now called synchronously on the auth path and returns the `ErrDeviceLimitReached` error. The service has a `localCache` meant to prevent repeated tagging (see `TestIntegrationAnonDeviceService_localCacheSafety`), but nothing in the shown diff suggests caching/backoff for the limit-reached error path, so repeated requests from blocked/new devices would continue to hit `CountDevices` + `UPDATE` each time. This is a concrete performance/operational concern introduced by the change, but not a correctness bug per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Bare ErrDeviceLimitReached returned from Authenticate with no defined HTTP mapping: it is a plain fmt.Errorf outside the authn error taxonomy, and behavior depends on how pkg/services/authn handles an unrecognized client error, potentially returning 500s instead of a graceful block/redirect

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` is defined as a plain `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` and is now synchronously propagated up to `Anonymous.Authenticate()` (client.go) via `TagDevice()` (impl.go now `return err`). `Authenticate` returns `nil, err` when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`. However, the diff does not show any wrapping into an authn-specific error type or any explicit HTTP/status mapping for this new error, so how it will be translated into a response is unclear from the diff alone. The specific claim about it causing 500s depends on authn internals not shown here, but the lack of taxonomy/mapping for a newly propagated error is a concrete review concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: rowsAffected == 0 conflates 'not found', 'stale', and 'no-op update' in updateDevice: on MySQL (second-precision DATETIME, affected-rows-not-found-rows semantics), two near-simultaneous tags of the same device produce identical row values, causing RowsAffected() == 0 and spurious ErrDeviceLimitReached for a device that exists and is in-window
matched_golden_ids: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core bug: updateDevice treats rowsAffected == 0 as a device-limit condition and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but 0 affected rows can occur for other reasons (device not found/outside time window or even a no-op update due to identical values/DB semantics).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Panic containment regression in the auth path: the defer recover() that guarded the tagging goroutine was removed with the goroutine itself, so a panic inside TagDevice/store code now propagates through Authenticate into the request handler and fails the request (500 via recovery middleware) instead of proceeding anonymously

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, Authenticate previously invoked TagDevice in a separate goroutine wrapped with a deferred recover(), so any panic in TagDevice or downstream store code would be contained and not affect the request. The diff removes the goroutine and the recover wrapper, and now calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously. Therefore a panic in TagDevice/store will now propagate through Authenticate into the request-handling goroutine, causing the request to fail (handled only by higher-level recovery middleware, if any), which is a behavior regression vs “proceed anonymously”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Core success path of the device limit feature is never tested: an existing, active device re-tagging itself once the limit is full is never exercised; updateDevice's success path (rowsAffected > 0) is never executed, so a regression in the SET clause, WHERE device_id match, or error/success branching would lock out every existing anonymous user while the suite stays green; the test also never asserts post-conditions (updated_at/client_ip/user_agent refresh, no duplicate row, device count stays at limit) (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51-69, database.go:72-115) [P1]

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial limit-handling logic in `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` that, when `count >= s.deviceLimit`, routes to `s.updateDevice(...)` (database.go). The only new test (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) hits the limit and then attempts to tag a *different* `DeviceID`, which makes `updateDevice`’s `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ? ...` affect 0 rows and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. There is no test that, once the limit is reached, re-tags an existing device so that `RowsAffected() > 0` (the success path of `updateDevice`) is executed, nor any assertions about post-conditions like updated fields, no duplicate row, and stable count at the limit. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap, not a confirmed runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The updated_at BETWEEN predicate in updateDevice is completely untested: in the only test reaching updateDevice, the incoming device_id never matches any row, so the test outcome is independent of the BETWEEN clause (inverted bounds, wrong constant, or wrong column would still pass); no test covers device_id matching with stored updated_at outside the 30-day window (should return ErrDeviceLimitReached) or inside it (should succeed) (database.go:74-84) [P2]

adjudication.rationale: In `database.go` the new `updateDevice` path enforces `WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` when `rowsAffected == 0`. The only added test that reaches this code (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) changes `DeviceID` to a value that was never inserted, so the UPDATE matches zero rows regardless of the `BETWEEN` bounds/window; the test would pass even if the `BETWEEN` clause were wrong. The diff shows no test covering the case where `device_id` exists but its stored `updated_at` is inside vs. outside the 30-day window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that expired devices stop counting toward the limit: no test creates a device with updated_at older than 30 days and verifies a new device can be created under a full-looking limit; if the CountDevices window regressed to counting all devices regardless of age, the limit would permanently freeze after the first N devices undetected (database.go:118-127) [P2]

adjudication.rationale: Diff introduces limit enforcement based on a 30-day window (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) by calling `CountDevices(ctx, now-30d, now+1m)` before insert/update (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go around the new CreateOrUpdateDevice precheck). The added test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers the “limit reached => new device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached” case with fresh (1h-old) devices, and does not cover that devices older than 30 days should fall outside the counted window and therefore not block creating a new device. That missing edge-case test is a specific gap in coverage for the new time-window logic, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavioral change in Authenticate (TagDevice moved from fire-and-forget goroutine to synchronous auth path, and ErrDeviceLimitReached now propagates out of Authenticate) has zero test work: no test verifies Authenticate returns the error when the limit is hit, the caller-visible outcome (401/429/500/fallthrough handling of this non-standard error in the authn pipeline), or that non-limit tagging errors still don't break authentication (client.go:35-52) [P1]
matched_golden_ids: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same behavioral change: TagDevice is no longer fire-and-forget, and ErrDeviceLimitReached now propagates out of Authenticate, which can cause anonymous authentication to fail when the device limit is hit. Although it emphasizes missing tests and downstream handling, it identifies the same underlying regression described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TagDevice now returns errors instead of swallowing them, but the new error contract is untested: updated TestIntegrationDeviceService_tag cases only assert require.NoError on success paths; no test asserts errors are returned to the caller (e.g., invalid/short device ID cookie), leaving callers relying on the old never-fail behavior unprotected (impl.go:143-150) [P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes TagDevice to propagate errors from tagDeviceUI: in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go it now `return err` after logging (previously it would just log and continue). However, the updated integration tests (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl_test.go) still only assert `require.NoError` on the exercised paths and do not add any test that verifies an error is returned to the caller when tagging fails. The finding’s example (invalid/short device ID cookie) isn’t shown in this diff, but the core point—newly propagated error behavior lacks coverage—is grounded in the change at impl.go:143+ and the absence of corresponding negative tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Config wiring (device_limit ini → Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit → ProvideAnonDBStore) is untested end-to-end: service-level tests use setting.NewCfg() (limit defaults to 0 = disabled) and the store-level test passes the limit directly, bypassing the wiring; a regression that always passes 0 (silently disabling the feature) would be invisible to the suite; negative values silently treated as 'no limit' are also untested/undocumented (setting.go:1649-1655, impl.go:37-42) [P2]

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ini wiring `auth.anonymous.device_limit` → `Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` (setting.go) and uses it when constructing the store inside `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` via `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)` (impl.go). However, the service-level integration tests invoke `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService(..., store, setting.NewCfg(), ...)` without setting `AnonymousDeviceLimit`, so they only exercise the default `0` (feature disabled) path. The new store-level test (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) passes the limit directly to `ProvideAnonDBStore(store, 1)`, bypassing the config/service wiring. Thus a regression where the service always passes `0` would not be caught. Also, negative values are effectively treated as "no limit" because enforcement is guarded by `if s.deviceLimit > 0` (database.go) and there is no test/documentation for that behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Count-then-insert race in CreateOrUpdateDevice allows exceeding the limit: CountDevices and the insert run as separate, non-transactional statements, so concurrent requests when count == limit-1 can both observe count < limit and both insert; no test documents or exercises concurrent behavior (database.go:118-127) [P3]

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the new device-limit enforcement does `CountDevices(...)` and, if below the limit, proceeds to insert/update the device in a separate DB session/statement. There’s no transaction/locking tying the count to the subsequent insert path, so concurrent requests can both observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and both insert, exceeding the configured limit. The added test (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) is single-threaded and doesn’t cover this concurrency case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Zero-rows-affected conflation ('no match' vs 'no change') untested under MySQL semantics: rowsAffected == 0 is mapped to ErrDeviceLimitReached, but on MySQL an UPDATE matching a row yet changing no values reports 0 affected rows (without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS), so a device re-tagging with identical client_ip/user_agent and unchanged second-precision updated_at could be falsely rejected; no test covers re-tagging an existing device with unchanged values (database.go:92-101) [P3]

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (database.go) an `UPDATE` is executed and `rowsAffected == 0` is treated as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. This conflates “no matching row” with “matching row but no data changed”. With MySQL’s default affected-rows semantics (without `CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS`), an UPDATE that matches a row but sets identical values can report 0 affected rows, causing a legitimate re-tag/update to be incorrectly rejected as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. The diff adds no test covering re-tagging an existing device where values (incl. DB-truncated timestamps) don’t change, so this edge case is unguarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Device limit is bypassed by a simple retry — TagDevice writes the device to the local cache (SetDefaultInt64) before the DB write, so a rejected write (ErrDeviceLimitReached) leaves the device cached; subsequent requests hit the cache and succeed without touching the DB, letting blocked devices in for the 29-minute cache window
matched_golden_ids: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same flaw: the device ID is cached before the CreateOrUpdate/DB write, and if ErrDeviceLimitReached occurs the cache entry remains, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the ~29-minute cache TTL expires.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice — CountDevices and the INSERT run in separate sessions with no transaction, lock, or admission record, so concurrent first-tags from multiple new devices all read count < limit and all insert, overshooting the limit

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, the admission check is `CountDevices(...)` followed by an INSERT/UPSERT in a later DB session (`CountDevices` and the eventual write are not wrapped in a single transaction or protected by a lock). With concurrent first-time tags from multiple new devices, each goroutine can observe `count < s.deviceLimit` and then proceed to insert, allowing the total to exceed `deviceLimit`. This race is directly implied by the separated count-then-write flow added in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Anonymous authentication now performs synchronous DB I/O in the request path — the fire-and-forget goroutine (context.Background + 2-minute timeout + panic recovery) was removed unconditionally, so every cache-cold anonymous request blocks on CountDevices (a COUNT over anon_device with no index on updated_at) plus the upsert with no explicit timeout, even when device_limit = 0

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the fire-and-forget goroutine in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` and now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` synchronously in `Authenticate`, which can introduce request-path latency and no longer enforces the previous explicit 2-minute timeout/panic recovery wrapper. However, the finding overstates that this causes a `CountDevices` on every cache-cold request "even when device_limit = 0"—`CountDevices` is only executed when `s.deviceLimit > 0` in `CreateOrUpdateDevice`. Claims about missing DB indexes on `updated_at` are not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: ErrDeviceLimitReached never reaches the user — the authn service logs client errors and continues to the next client, ultimately failing with a generic 'credentials missing' 401/redirect to login, so blocked users get no explanation and operators cannot distinguish limit-reached from an auth outage; the anonymousDeviceLimit frontend field is unused for messaging

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the opposite: `Anonymous.Authenticate` now calls `TagDevice` synchronously and explicitly returns the error when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go), and `TagDevice` was changed to `return err` on UI tagging failures (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go), so `ErrDeviceLimitReached` does propagate upward. The claim that the authn service will just log and continue to another client and end with a generic 401/redirect is not verifiable from this diff. While `anonymousDeviceLimit` is added to config/DTO and not used for messaging in this diff, the finding’s core assertion (“never reaches the user”) conflicts with the shown code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: rowsAffected == 0 is overloaded in updateDevice — on MySQL (default changed-rows semantics, second-precision DATETIME), an UPDATE matching an existing fresh device can round to the same stored second (e.g., same device tagged on two instances within the same second) and report 0 affected rows, falsely rejecting the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice`, the code treats `rowsAffected == 0` as “device not updated” and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). But the UPDATE sets `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at` to values derived from the incoming `device`; if the stored row already has the same values (notably if `updated_at` is stored with lower precision and the new timestamp rounds/truncates to the same stored value), some DBs/drivers (notably MySQL with changed-rows semantics) can report 0 affected rows even when a row matched the WHERE clause. That would incorrectly reject an existing device when the limit is reached.
